text:
Mackie Samoskevich has made the move from Florida to Seattle look like a promotion. He has 15 points in 21 games, nearly half of last season's 32, and FOX 13 Seattle credits him and Matty Beniers with "fueling Kraken's fast offensive start." He has assists in four of his last six games, including the backdoor feed to Beniers on November 22.

How much is real? A fair amount. The Kraken take 49.9% of the expected goals (the quality of chances) with him on at five on five, which sounds ordinary until you see it's 6.2 points better than when he sits. Evolving-Hockey had him 90th percentile among forwards in driving offense last season, and Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had him exiting with possession 70% of the time, with 53% of his shots coming off the rush. He's a transition player on a team that's learning to play fast.

The point rate (2.7 per 60) is above what our talent range expects (about 2.0), so some cooling is likely. The Stanley Cup ring from 2025 came as a depth piece. In Seattle he's a featured one.
